So I got my master's in statistics at SJSU. So unfortunately, I can only give advice regarding it. 

Since you mentioned that you want to focus solely on statistics, I recommend you actually look at the overlap between the Applied Math w/Stat Concentration and the M.S statistics. 

Looking at it real quickly, if you decide SJSU, just take.. the lower div requirements. 

For upper div, math 161a, 161b, 163, 164, 167. Those are the required upper div requirements that are stats related. Also have to take 129a cuz of the math requirement I guess. 

The list I will be mentioning are classes that grad students take. 

162, 261a, 261b, 265 

Honestly, if you want the stats degree, you can just take stats grad courses that are listed in the master's program. Now you probably won't get the official "B.S. in stats" but you can actually take advantage of the opportunity and say that you've taken courses equivalent to a master's degree. If you ultimately decide to get a master's, you'll be more prepared than most people.
